lessons.title: Qu'est-ce qu'un quartier?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand what a neighborhood is and identify the basic elements that make up their local area

opening.activity: Neighborhood circle where students share one thing they see when they walk outside their home. Introduce the word 'quartier' with welcoming, expansive gestures that suggest community connection.
opening.visualSupports: Open arms for community inclusion, pointing gestures for exploration, wide circle for neighborhood concept
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne connaît pas le mot 'quartier' → utiliser des gestes qui montrent 'autour de nous' et pointer vers les fenêtres pour montrer l'extérieur
Si un élève dit qu'il n'aime pas son quartier → rassurer qu'on peut toujours trouver quelque chose de bien et commencer par identifier une chose positive
Si un élève veut parler de lieux dangereux → rediriger vers les endroits sécuritaires et les personnes qui aident dans le quartier
movementBreaks: Marcher en syllabant notre nom : Ma-rie, Paul, etc. en tapant dans nos mains (2 minutes)
Faire l'alphabet avec notre corps : A comme arbre (étirer les bras), B comme ballon (forme ronde) (3 minutes)

main.activity: Neighborhood exploration using aerial photos and neighborhood picture books. Students create a 'What Makes a Neighborhood' anchor chart, identifying homes, streets, people, and places. Build understanding that neighborhoods are collections of homes where people live together as a community.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to neighborhood elements, building gestures for homes, walking motions for streets, people connections for community

decisionPoints.question: How familiar are students with their immediate neighborhood?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use specific local examples and encourage students to share familiar places
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use general neighborhood concepts and focus on universal elements like homes and streets

decisionPoints.question: Should we start with the school area or students' home areas?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Begin with school neighborhood since it's shared experience
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with home neighborhoods to build personal connection first

movementBreaks: Danser avec les sons : 'a' avec les bras, 'o' en rond, 'i' pointu (3 minutes)
Marcher sur place en récitant l'alphabet lentement (2 minutes)

closing.activity: Neighborhood appreciation circle where students share one word that describes their neighborhood. End with group chant: 'Mon quartier est spécial!'
materials: boîte de rangement pour travaux (1 grande boîte)
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne peut pas penser à un mot pour décrire son quartier → suggérer des mots simples comme 'bon', 'calme', ou 'grand'
Si un élève utilise des mots négatifs → accepter ses sentiments et ajouter quelque chose de positif comme 'et aussi...'
movementBreaks: Célébrer nos apprentissages : applaudir, lever les bras, sourire (2 minutes)
Ranger nos idées : faire semblant de mettre nos pensées dans une boîte (2 minutes)

lessons.title: Ma maison dans mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will locate their home within their neighborhood and understand their place in the local community

opening.activity: Home location circle where students point in the direction of their home and say 'Ma maison est là-bas' (My house is over there). Practice confident pointing and proud expressions about home location.
opening.visualSupports: Confident pointing gestures, proud posture, directional movements
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne sait pas où il habite → commencer par identifier des repères qu'il connaît près de l'école
Si un élève confond 'maison' et 'quartier' → utiliser ses mains pour montrer 'petit' pour maison et 'grand' pour quartier

decisionPoints.question: Si un élève partage une structure familiale diverse
decisionPoints.ifYes: Célébrer la diversité: 'Quelle belle famille unique!'
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continuer avec respect pour toutes les familles

movementBreaks: Imiter les animaux des histoires : sauter comme un lapin, voler comme un oiseau (3 minutes)
Former des lettres dans l'air avec nos doigts : A, B, C (3 minutes)

main.activity: Home mapping activity using simple neighborhood maps and address practice. Students locate their street or area on a neighborhood map and create a personal 'My Home in My Neighborhood' drawing showing their house connected to the school and other important places.
materials: Images de familles diverses (monoparentales, recomposées, multiculturelles)
main.visualSupports: Pointing to map locations, connecting lines between places, home symbols, pathway gestures

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students sharing their address information?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use real street names and help students practice their address
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use example addresses and focus on general neighborhood location concepts

decisionPoints.question: How do we handle students with temporary or unstable housing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on current location and emphasize that home is where family is together
decisionPoints.ifNo: Celebrate all types of homes and housing situations equally

movementBreaks: Faire une pause lecture : s'étirer comme un chat qui se réveille (2 minutes)
Marcher sur place en récitant l'alphabet lentement (2 minutes)

closing.activity: Home connection sharing where students show their drawings and share one thing they like about where their home is located. Celebrate all locations as special.
materials: lingettes pour nettoyer les mains (1 paquet)
decisionPoints: Si un élève dit 'Je ne sais pas mon adresse' → rassurer que c'est normal et qu'on peut commencer par des repères qu'il connaît
Si un élève veut dire son adresse complète → l'encourager mais garder le focus sur les concepts généraux pour tous
movementBreaks: Dire au revoir avec tout notre corps : mains, têtes, pieds (2 minutes)
Faire une révérence à nos nouvelles connaissances (1 minute)

lessons.title: Les maisons de mes voisins
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore different types of homes in their neighborhood and understand housing diversity

opening.activity: Housing variety circle where students use their hands to show different house shapes (tall, wide, small, big) while saying 'Les maisons sont différentes' (Houses are different). Celebrate diversity with enthusiastic gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Varied hand shapes for different houses, celebratory expressions, inclusive arm movements
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne connaît pas ses voisins → expliquer qu'on peut quand même observer les maisons autour de nous
Si un élève veut parler de problèmes avec des voisins → rediriger vers l'observation respectueuse des différences

decisionPoints.question: Si un élève partage une structure familiale diverse
decisionPoints.ifYes: Célébrer la diversité: 'Quelle belle famille unique!'
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continuer avec respect pour toutes les familles

movementBreaks: Répéter des comptines avec gestes : 'Tête, épaules, genoux et pieds' (2 minutes)
Faire l'alphabet avec notre corps : A comme arbre (étirer les bras), B comme ballon (forme ronde) (3 minutes)

main.activity: Housing exploration using photos of different home types (houses, apartments, townhomes, mobile homes). Students create a 'Neighborhood Homes' collage showing various housing types and discuss how different families need different types of homes. Emphasize that all homes provide safety and belonging.
materials: Images de familles diverses (monoparentales, recomposées, multiculturelles)
main.visualSupports: Pointing to different house types with equal celebration, sheltering gestures, family inclusion movements

decisionPoints.question: How do we discuss housing differences without emphasizing socioeconomic disparities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on how different homes meet different family needs and preferences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize architectural features and family choice rather than economic factors

decisionPoints.question: How do we ensure all housing types are presented positively?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use enthusiastic language and highlight positive features of each housing type
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal home functions: safety, shelter, family togetherness

Étirer nos doigts et mains d'écrivains : ouvrir, fermer, tourner (2 minutes)

closing.activity: Home appreciation sharing where students share one positive thing about a different type of home they learned about. End with chant: 'Toutes les maisons sont importantes!'

lessons.title: Les rues de mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and understand the role of streets in connecting neighborhood places and people

opening.activity: Street movement circle where students practice walking, stopping, looking both ways, and connecting movements while saying 'Les rues nous connectent' (Streets connect us). Use safe walking gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Walking motions, stopping gestures, looking both ways, connecting hand movements
decisionPoints: Si un élève a peur de marcher dans certaines rues → discuter des adultes de confiance et des règles de sécurité
Si un élève veut explorer au-delà des limites → expliquer l'importance de rester dans notre zone sécuritaire
movementBreaks: Répéter des comptines avec gestes : 'Tête, épaules, genoux et pieds' (2 minutes)
Former des lettres dans l'air avec nos doigts : A, B, C (3 minutes)

main.activity: Street mapping activity using neighborhood street maps and street exploration. Students create a 'Street Connections' map showing how streets connect important places like home, school, stores, and parks. Practice identifying intersections and understanding that streets help people get where they need to go.
main.visualSupports: Tracing street paths with finger, connecting gestures between places, pathway movements

decisionPoints.question: What level of detail should we include about street safety?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include basic pedestrian safety concepts like looking both ways and using crosswalks
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on streets as connectors and save detailed safety for separate lessons

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on street names or general navigation concepts?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice some local street names that students might recognize
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on understanding streets as pathways rather than memorizing names

Étirer nos doigts et mains d'écrivains : ouvrir, fermer, tourner (2 minutes)

closing.activity: Street appreciation circle where students share one place they like to go on neighborhood streets. Practice safe walking movements together.

lessons.title: Promenade de sécurité dans le quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify safety features and practices for navigating their neighborhood

opening.activity: Safety superhero circle where students practice safety poses while saying safety phrases like 'Je regarde à gauche et à droite' (I look left and right). Use confident, alert body language.
opening.visualSupports: Alert posture, looking both ways, confident walking stance, protective gestures
decisionPoints: Si un élève a peur de marcher dans certaines rues → discuter des adultes de confiance et des règles de sécurité
Si un élève veut explorer au-delà des limites → expliquer l'importance de rester dans notre zone sécuritaire

Répéter des comptines avec gestes : 'Tête, épaules, genoux et pieds' (2 minutes)

main.activity: Guided neighborhood safety walk (or virtual tour if walking not possible) identifying safety features like crosswalks, stop signs, sidewalks, and trusted adult helpers. Students practice safe walking behaviors and create a 'Neighborhood Safety' checklist of important safety rules and features.

decisionPoints.question: Should we take an actual neighborhood walk or use virtual exploration?

decisionPoints.question: How do we teach safety without creating fear or anxiety?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Frame safety as smart, responsible behavior that helps us explore confidently

lessons.title: Les commerces près de chez moi
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify local businesses and understand how they serve neighborhood residents

opening.activity: Business discovery circle where students mime different shopping actions (buying food, getting hair cut, filling gas) while saying 'Les magasins nous aident' (Stores help us). Use helpful, service-oriented gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Service gestures, helping movements, shopping actions, community connection motions
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne connaît aucun commerce dans son quartier → commencer par identifier où sa famille fait les courses
Si un élève confond les types de commerces → utiliser des objets concrets pour clarifier (pain = boulangerie)
movementBreaks: Répéter des comptines avec gestes : 'Tête, épaules, genoux et pieds' (2 minutes)
Faire l'alphabet avec notre corps : A comme arbre (étirer les bras), B comme ballon (forme ronde) (3 minutes)

main.activity: Local business exploration using photos of neighborhood businesses and discussion of services they provide. Students create a 'Neighborhood Helpers' chart categorizing businesses by how they help families (food, clothing, services, health). Include businesses from students' experiences.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to business services, categorizing gestures, helping movements, community connections

decisionPoints.question: Which local businesses are most familiar to students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with businesses students know and expand to others they might not have visited
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use universal business types that exist in most communities

decisionPoints.question: How do we represent businesses students may not be able to afford to visit?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on the services they provide to the community rather than personal shopping experiences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize that all businesses help make neighborhoods complete and serve different needs

Étirer nos doigts et mains d'écrivains : ouvrir, fermer, tourner (2 minutes)

closing.activity: Business appreciation circle where students share one neighborhood business they would like to learn more about and why it's helpful to families.

lessons.title: Qui travaille dans mon quartier?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize various workers in their neighborhood and understand how jobs support community life

opening.activity: Community workers circle where students mime different neighborhood jobs (mail delivery, bus driving, store clerk) while saying 'Les travailleurs nous aident' (Workers help us). Use appreciative, respectful gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Job-specific movements, helping gestures, respectful acknowledgment, community service motions
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne reconnaît aucun travailleur du quartier → commencer par les personnes à l'école comme exemples
Si un élève veut parler du travail de ses parents → l'encourager mais maintenir le focus sur les travailleurs visibles dans le quartier
movementBreaks: Former des lettres dans l'air avec nos doigts : A, B, C (3 minutes)
Marcher en syllabant notre nom : Ma-rie, Paul, etc. en tapant dans nos mains (2 minutes)

main.activity: Neighborhood workers exploration using photos and stories of local workers. Students create a 'Community Helpers' book with pages for different neighborhood workers, showing how each job helps families and neighbors. Include both formal and informal community helpers.
main.visualSupports: Demonstrating job actions, appreciative pointing, community connection gestures, helpful movements

decisionPoints.question: Which neighborhood workers are most visible and relatable to students?

decisionPoints.ifNo: Include a variety of workers and explain how all jobs contribute to community life

decisionPoints.question: How do we present all types of work as valuable and important?

decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on how every worker helps make the neighborhood function well

lessons.title: Les services publics de mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify public services in their neighborhood and understand how they benefit everyone

opening.activity: Public service circle where students practice sharing gestures while saying 'C'est pour tout le monde' (It's for everyone). Use inclusive, welcoming movements that show community sharing.
opening.visualSupports: Sharing gestures, inclusive arm movements, welcoming expressions, community gathering motions
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne comprend pas ce que sont les services publics → utiliser des exemples concrets qu'il voit chaque jour
Si un élève demande pourquoi on a besoin de ces services → expliquer simplement comment ils aident les familles

Cordialement,
